blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 25 in June to 18 in October (−28.0%), and it took 12.1% of the city’s 141 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Hatzic for detached houses in June, July, September, October (a sellers’ best bet).

items.t: Hatzic is three places under one mailing name: the Hatzic Bench inside the City of Mission, Hatzic Prairie in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area F, and Hatzic Island in Electoral Area G. The FVRD lists Area F as McConnell Creek and Hatzic Prairie, and Area G as Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney and Hatzic Island
Bench streets inside the City include Ferguson Avenue, Jasper Avenue, McEwen Avenue, Ferndale Avenue and Dewdney Trunk Road, while Shook Road serves the Hatzic Lake and Hatzic Island side
The Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 0999, 2010, covers the Area F valley floor between Hatzic Lake and Stave Lake, including Hatzic Prairie and Durieu

The Bench holds city-lot houses near Hatzic Elementary and Hatzic Middle School, while the lake side on Shook Road holds cabins, park homes and resort use-area lots — three tenure types on one guide page
Hatzic Prairie holds farm and acreage housing on valley-floor parcels, most of the inhabited valley being in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) with commercial and hobby farming

Which rulebook applies depends on which side of the City and FVRD line the parcel sits on: City of Mission zoning and suite registration on the Bench, FVRD Bylaw No. 0999, 2010 and FVRD Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 on the Prairie, confirmed parcel by parcel

Inside the City, all secondary suites must be registered with the City and suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhouses; in Electoral Area F, a suite must sit inside the main house and cannot be a detached garden suite
Flood protection here is run by the Dewdney Area Improvement District (DAID), which owns and operates the Hatzic pump station and electrical kiosks in Hatzic Slough, per the FVRD's joint release

blocks.text: Hatzic: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Hatzic Prairie water is billed twice a year, not monthly: the FVRD's 2026 Area F rates list Water – Hatzic Prairie (service 491) as metered, billed semi-annually in April and October, with a $335.00 minimum charge
The Hatzic Lake pump station was rebuilt with three submersible fish-friendly pumps from Bedford Pumps, the first of that type installed in the Lower Fraser, serving the whole Hatzic Lake watershed
A local state of emergency was declared for the Hatzic Lake area during the November 2021 atmospheric river, which is the event the current pump and watershed funding follows
Neilson Regional Park, an FVRD regional park on the west side of Hatzic Lake, is the lake's named public park in the FVRD parks snapshot
The Hatzic Watershed Stewardship Team behind the flood work includes Leq'á:mel First Nation, the FVRD, the DAID, the City of Mission and provincial ministries
The Hatzic Prairie water charge in ($335.00 semi-annual minimum, 2026, service 491) is the sub-area-specific utility cost here

The West Coast Express runs from Mission City Station with five weekday westbound trains at 5:25 to 7:25 a.m. reaching Waterfront in 75 minutes, five eastbound returns and no weekend service, per the TransLink timetable

BC Transit and the FVRD consulted in spring 2025 on a proposed Highway 7 bus between Mission and Agassiz that would serve the Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway corridor south of Hatzic if funded

Check flood status, dike protection and flood-construction level by PID for any Prairie, Island or Shook Road lot, because the 1948 dyke break flooded the Prairie and the 2021 atmospheric river brought a local state of emergency at Hatzic Lake
Check whether the lot sits behind DAID dike works or outside them, and confirm any DAID parcel tax or drainage charge for the PID with the improvement district
Check ALR status by PID on the Agricultural Land Commission maps, because most inhabited Prairie land is in the ALR and ALR status controls second homes and subdivision

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Hatzic Mission than in June?
faq.a: In Hatzic Mission, listings of houses fell from 25 in June to 18 in October (−28.0%).

faq.q: How big is Hatzic Mission compared with the rest of Mission?
faq.a: In October 2026, Hatzic Mission held 8.3% of the 216 houses listed in Mission.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Hatzic Mission from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 17 houses sold in Hatzic Mission over those 5 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Hatzic Mission?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.
